cards.notes: Owner-approved quarantine 2026-07-27: skipped on CI only (test.skip(!!process.env.CI, ...)) because GitHub shared runners degraded 24h+ (7s local -> ~186s CI). Runs+passes locally. Delete the test.skip line when runners recover. Tracked in docs/QUESTIONS.md. UN-QUARANTINED 2026-07-31, and the 2026-07-27 diagnosis was WRONG. Re-enabling it failed CI three times for three identical minutes, and the Playwright artifact named the real cause: "element is not stable ... element was detached from the DOM, retrying" for the full 180s. Not slowness - a RACE. Every write in that spec is a server action ending in redirect("/admin/staff?m=<code>"), and the test waited with waitForURL(/admin\/staff/), a pattern the CURRENT url already satisfies, so it waited for nothing and the next click landed in the outgoing DOM that the redirect was about to replace. Locally the race is won and the test passes in 7s, which is exactly why it looked like an infra problem: same symptom, opposite cause. Fixed by waiting on the app's own signals - the redirect's ?m= marker plus the rendered banner - instead of a regex that was already true. The 180s per-test budget stays; it was never the quarantine. CLAIM RETRACTED 2026-08-02. This card was marked SHIPPED on #730 and that was WRONG - the quarantine has been REINSTATED on main by #739. GREENs error was the standard of proof, not the diagnosis: #730 was shipped on ONE green CI run with retries enabled, which for a RACY test proves nothing (retries mask precisely the failure being tested, and a single sample cannot separate fixed from lucky). The PR even called that run the proof. A parallel session then measured it properly - the spec alone, twice each, at --retries=0, on clean origin/main AND on an unrelated apps/api branch - and all four runs failed with the same detach race #730 claimed to fix. Failing on CLEAN MAIN is the decisive part: the cause is in this spec or the surface it drives, not in any pending branch. The DIAGNOSIS still stands (a race; the open-blocks button is found, then detaches between resolve and click, burning the full 180s) and settleAfterWrite fixed the writes GREEN could see - something else on that surface still remounts. NEW EXIT CONDITION, from #739 and stricter than the one GREEN used: two CONSECUTIVE green runs at --retries=0, not a hunch and not one lucky pass. cards.title: Never ask for what the patient record already holds - NIF applied automatically, then a sweep of every re-asking form
cards.notes: Owner CR 2026-07-31: "there are still input forms on the platform where it is directly client related or started to be done from the patient profile, for example the declaracao document asks for NIF again although it was filled at the time of adding the patient, need to automate all these cases and don't even ask to input but auto fill and reflect at the result, bring more automation and logic, cannot be limited to NIF only". Work: apply the PL-14 shape to patient data - a KNOWN value is a static line, not an input; an UNKNOWN value is asked once and what is entered is written BACK to the patient record so it is never asked a third time; an explicit 'alterar' affordance keeps the one-off override. Then sweep every form that re-asks something the patient row already carries (nome, NIF, data de nascimento, morada, telefone across documents and invoicing) and report what was found rather than guessing the list up front. The write-back is a patients:write path reception already holds. SWEEP RESULT: the declaracao NIF is the ONLY surface in the staff platform that re-asks a field the patient record already holds. Faturacao reads name/NIF/address from the patient through the InvoiceXpress mapper, the RGPD form and ficha medica are generated from the record, and Reagendar / Marcar novamente already reuse the marcacao's own therapist and location. cards.title: Portal booking is on the hour - a patient can only pick 09:00, 10:00, 11:00
cards.notes: Owner CR 2026-07-31: "users should only be able to clock in/out on the hour, for example at 9:00, 10:00 - here we need to make sure on our client portal that for them the only option to book appointments is fixed hourly, they can't book at :15th minute or half of hour". FINDING: the portal never fabricates slots - they come from GET /api/v1/booking/slots -> listOpenSlots (apps/api/lib/appointments/store.ts:325), which expands each active availability template into a grid stepped by locations.slot_granularity_min (migration 0041, default 30). TWO things are needed, not one: (a) the step becomes 60, and (b) the grid must be ALIGNED to the top of the hour - the series starts at the template's own start_time, so a therapist whose hours begin 09:30 would still produce 09:30 / 10:30 at a 60-minute step. The alignment half is code and self-merges; changing the stored granularity per location is data and is hard-gated. Staff-side booking is deliberately UNCHANGED - the agenda keeps free-form times, this constrains only what a patient may self-serve. Nothing in the product edits slot_granularity_min from the UI today. Q-PL-25-1 logged for whether hourly applies to every location. PROD READ 2026-08-02 corrects two things GREEN asserted. (1) BOTH clinics were ALREADY at slot_granularity_min = 60 before this session - GREEN said they sat at 30 and would need switching, inferring that from the 0041 default instead of reading prod. Patient booking was already hourly; no toggle is pending. (2) The alignment half was LOAD-BEARING, not theoretical: Linda-a-Velha has 10 ACTIVE availability templates starting off the hour (08:30 and 13:30). At a 60-minute step without alignment those emitted 08:30 / 09:30 / 10:30 - an hourly cadence never landing on an hour, exactly the trap PL-25 describes. Castelo Branco has 0 off-hour starts, so CB was unaffected either way. CONSEQUENCE worth knowing: with alignment, an 08:30 LV template now offers 09:00 first, so LV patients lose the 08:30 self-serve start. That is inherent to hourly booking and staff can still book 08:30 from the agenda.

cards.title: Reception can block the schedule from the AGENDA, and repeat it - stale settings:manage gate hid an existing control
cards.notes: Owner report 2026-07-31, after PL-22 shipped: 'reception still doesn't have batch schedule block, same as you made in the new appointment panel, also reception doesn't have that button I have for example to press there in agenda bloquear horario and in agenda she can block something in the day, it's something existent but not visible on their interface for now'. TWO symptoms, ONE root cause, and the owner's reading of it is exactly right - the feature exists and the interface hides it. FINDING: agenda/page.tsx gated the Bloquear horario affordance on settings:manage, which owner and admin hold and reception does NOT. That gate was CORRECT when W12-28 shipped it, and went stale at PL-09 Phase 5, which created the explicit schedule:manage capability, granted it to reception ('reception OWNS scheduling for their location's therapists'), and moved every time_off write onto it. The server has asserted schedule:manage ever since; only the UI check was left behind, and its own comment still claimed the two were 'the SAME capability createTimeOffBlock server-enforces' - a claim that stopped being true and was never re-read. So reception could always have blocked time; nothing in the agenda ever offered it to them. SECOND HALF: PL-22 put bulk blocking only in the per-therapist Bloquear horario modal on Horarios/Equipa. The agenda is where the day is actually managed, so from where reception works, batch blocking did not exist - which is why the owner reports it missing even though PL-22 merged. The agenda dialog now offers Repetir bloqueio using the SAME generateLoteSchedule + createTimeOffBlockBatch, so all three recurrence forms (agendar lote, bloquear lote, agenda block) behave identically. No migration, no capability change, no relaxed guard: the server re-asserts schedule:manage AND the location scope (resolveScheduleScope + assertTargetInScheduleScope), so reception can only block a therapist at their own clinic. SHIPPED (#729, no migration). The gate now reads schedule:manage, matching what createTimeOffBlock actually asserts, and the agenda dialog gained 'Repetir bloqueio' driven by the same generateLoteSchedule + createTimeOffBlockBatch as Agendar lote and the Horarios modal - three recurrence forms, one generator, so they cannot drift. The test added is an INVARIANT (whoever may WRITE a block is who may SEE the control), so a future regate breaks a test instead of silently hiding a control again.

cards.title: Board portal showed a stale board with no warning - staleness compared DATES, so same-day republishes were invisible
cards.notes: Owner report 2026-08-02 with a screenshot: the portal showed PL-18..PL-25 as TO DO with 'no evidence yet' and Shipped 22, while main had them shipped with PR evidence and Shipped 30. GREEN's bug, and a bad one, because the owner reviews ALL work through this artifact - he was reading a board that said nothing had shipped. ROOT CAUSE: seedIsNewer() compared as_of DATES (SEED.as_of > board.as_of). Every publish on 2026-07-31 carried as_of '2026-07-31', so the comparison was false for all FOUR publishes that day and the 'newer board' notice never rendered. Worse, the 'Load the new board' button lives INSIDE that notice, so the one control that would have fixed it was unreachable; only the footer's 'Discard local changes' remained, which also throws away the owner's own edits. A date cannot express 'changed again today'. FIX: render-board.mjs now stamps a sha256 content fingerprint of the published JSON into the seed island, and the portal records which publish a browser's snapshot was taken from (__basedOn in localStorage, kept beside the board so it never leaks into an Export or a diff). Staleness is now fingerprint inequality, which catches ANY change - status, evidence, a note - same day or not. A pre-fix snapshot has no recorded provenance and is treated as STALE, so every browser stranded by the old logic is offered the new board on first load. Adopting the seed (take-seed and Discard) also adopts its fingerprint, or the notice would return on the board the user just chose. VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER against a reproduction of the owner's exact state (a snapshot showing Shipped 22, same as_of, no provenance): notice appears where it previously did not; 'Load the new board' clears it and survives a reload showing Shipped 30; and a CURRENT snapshot carrying local edits is not falsely flagged (1 local change preserved, no notice). LESSON: a freshness check keyed on a human-scale date silently fails at human speed - version by content, not by calendar. SHIPPED (#732). The very publish that carries this card is also the first one a stranded browser can detect, because a pre-fix snapshot has no recorded provenance and is therefore treated as stale.

cards.title: Patient portal accepted UNVERIFIED tokens - anyone could impersonate any patient (SHIPPED #735)
cards.notes: SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (#735), merged on fully green CI - all eight checks SUCCESS including the Playwright re-run at 20:07 once the #739 quarantine landed. NOT GREENs work; recorded here because the board is the launch record and this is the most serious defect found in the run-up. WHAT IT WAS: the patient API read the identity token a caller presented and TRUSTED it without verifying the signature. Anyone on the internet could mint a token naming any patient and be admitted as that patient - full read of another persons clinical data, under GDPR. WHY THE STATED SAFETY NET WAS NOT ONE: the code claimed RLS would catch a forged token. It could not - RLS resolves the patient identity FROM THE SAME UNVERIFIED TOKEN, so it compared the forgery against itself and agreed. Those comments were deleted rather than left describing protection that never existed. FIX: real ES256 signature verification against the projects published public key (there was never a secret to be missing - only a public key to fetch), plus rate limiting on the patient surface, with tests including an explicit forged-token case. RELEVANCE NOW: the owner is about to work on the client portal and SMS/email. This closed a hole in exactly that surface, and the patient portal is the one surface reachable by people who are not staff.

cards.title: marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts:178 fails intermittently across unrelated branches - diagnose before it blocks a merge

evidence.ref: FULL suite at --retries=0 on the fix branch, run 30986393217: green, with BOTH colliding specs executing in the same run. Retries=0 matters because retries were what hid this for weeks. PR #789. Root cause proved from the failure VIDEO of run 30827445090 (frame at t~1.5s shows the appointment already on the agenda BEFORE any submit), corroborated by three independent reads: no reminder-enqueue log lines in the failing window while all 35 committed bookings in that run emit one; createAppointment returns on conflict BEFORE its INSERT; and the spec that books first passed with a single click, proving the slot was empty when it ran.

cards.notes:
Raised 2026-08-02. PL-02 (a) reschedule from the Marcacoes tab has now failed on at least THREE separate CI runs on unrelated branches (#724 PL-20, #735 security W1, and the run before the therapist-blocks quarantine landed). GREEN called it flake the first time, on the reasoning that it passed on sibling PRs off the same base - which was true then and is no longer a sufficient argument at three strikes across unrelated work. Failure signature: expect(dialog).toBeHidden({timeout: 12000}) fails with unexpected value visible at line 55 of the helper - the appointment dialog does not close after a save. That is the SAME family as the therapist-blocks race (a dialog/redirect not settling before the next assertion), so the two may share one cause and one fix. NOT diagnosed yet and deliberately not guessed: the lesson from LE-ci-quarantine-reenable is that one green run proves nothing about a racy test. Reproduce it the way #739 did - the spec alone, repeatedly, at --retries=0 - before proposing anything. INVESTIGATED 2026-08-03, NOT yet root-caused - recorded rather than guessed. FAILING ASSERTION located: it is not the reschedule at line 178 at all, it is expect(dialog).toBeHidden({timeout:12000}) inside the book() HELPER at line 55 - the CREATE dialog does not close within 12s after Guardar. A dialog that stays open after save is the shape of a REFUSED save (a conflict banner keeps it open), not of a slow one. WHY IT SELF-HEALS: each test derives its day from bandDay(base, testInfo.retry) which shifts +100 days PER RETRY, so attempt 2 books on a day nothing else touches and passes. That is also why it never fails twice - the retry changes the input, so retries here do not merely re-run, they CHANGE THE TEST. RULED OUT: the therapist-blocks working-hours mutation fixed in #752 - marcacoes still flaked in the very run that merged that fix (failed one attempt, passed on retry, 166 passed). DAY-BAND MAP built across the whole suite: marcacoes uses +40,+41,+42,+44,+45; therapist-blocks creates a PROLONGADA absence spanning +40..+42 for the same therapist and clears it at the end; therapist-self-lock uses +44. The failing attempt used +45, which no other spec claims - so a naive day collision does NOT explain it and the obvious answer is wrong. NEXT STEP, deliberately not taken on a hunch: capture the actual reason the save is refused. The dialog is still on screen at failure, so the Playwright artifact for that attempt carries the conflict text - read test-failed-1.png / error-context.md from a failing run rather than reasoning about which day should be free. NOT BLOCKING: it passes on retry, so it has never failed a gate outright; it costs ~3 wasted CI minutes each time. ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED 2026-08-03, from the ARTIFACT rather than from reasoning - and the answer was none of the three theories. The captured page state shows the drawer still open carrying "O terapeuta nao tem horario de trabalho definido neste dia." and a "Guardar mesmo assim" button. The save was never slow and never conflicted: it was ADVISORY-GATED. PL-11 made availability warn rather than block, so booking a therapist on a day they do not work keeps the drawer open awaiting an explicit confirm, and book() clicked Guardar once and asserted the drawer had closed. NOT RANDOM, DATE-DEPENDENT: bandDay derives a calendar DATE, so RUN_DAY_BASE+45 falls on a different WEEKDAY depending on when the suite runs - on a working weekday one click saves, otherwise the advisory appears. The +100-day retry offset shifts the weekday by two (100 mod 7), which is why attempt 2 passed and why this looked like flake for a week: the retry CHANGED THE INPUT rather than re-running the test. It would have failed reliably on certain calendar dates and never on others. FIX: book() confirms the advisory when it is present, mirroring what a user does and the pattern already in agenda-cards.spec.ts. Verified locally at --retries=0: 9 passed. LESSON, the same one three times this week: the Playwright artifact NAMES the cause in plain text; every theory formed without reading it was wrong.

RE-OPENED 2026-08-03 ON EVIDENCE, hours after being marked shipped. While reviewing a PL-31 CI failure I could not attribute, I triggered a CONTROL E2E run on main (run 30827445090) carrying none of my changes. It FAILED, on this exact test: marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts:196, inside book(), on the same `await expect(dialog).toBeHidden()` this card says it fixed.

So the fix is incomplete. The advisory-confirm the card added does handle the 'terapeuta nao tem horario' path, and that diagnosis still looks right - but something ELSE also keeps the drawer open on some calendar dates, and one green local run at --retries=0 could not have shown it, because the input changes with the date. That is this board's own rule, written on another card this week: one green run proves nothing about anything that can race.

NOT A PL-31 REGRESSION, and that is established rather than assumed: this spec never creates a patient and never touches the NIF path, and the control run above fails on main without any PL-31 code. The PL-31 branch's own E2E then passed, so it is intermittent within a single day too.

STATUS deliberately returned to todo with evidence CLEARED. It was marked shipped on a receipt that was real but insufficient (9 local passes at retries=0), and leaving the receipt attached would let the next reader think the question is settled. NEXT STEP for whoever takes it: read the error-context.md from run 30827445090 FIRST - do not theorise - and look for a SECOND blocking dialog state beyond the working-hours advisory.

PARTIAL FIX IN PR #761, card DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. The artifact from control run 30827445090 was read before anything was changed. Two defects in book() are provable and are fixed:
  1. isVisible() DOES NOT AUTO-WAIT in Playwright - it is an immediate poll, so the old code asked whether the override button had appeared microseconds after clicking Guardar, before the server had answered. It read false, skipped the confirm, then sat in toBeHidden watching a drawer that was waiting for exactly the click it had just decided not to make.
  2. getByRole name matching is SUBSTRING by default, so { name: 'Guardar' } also matches 'Guardar mesmo assim' once the label flips. Pinned with exact:true. The reschedule cases in the same file already used an anchored regex for this reason, so the hazard was known.
Also corrected a FALSE STATEMENT in this spec's own comment: the working-hours advisory is not a separate mechanism from conflicts - it arrives as a conflicts entry of kind 'availability', and any non-null conflicts flips the confirm label (appointment-drawer.tsx:727). A comment that misdescribes the mechanism is how the next reader gets sent down the wrong path.

WHY STILL OPEN: the failure screenshot shows the appointment HAD been created while the drawer stayed open in the override state, and neither defect above explains that. Do not close this on one green run.

CLOSED 2026-08-05. ROOT CAUSE: a day collision between two specs, not a race and not a product defect.

marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts and marcacao-patient-link.spec.ts:31 both used bandDay(45), and BOTH book PATIENTS.maria with THERAPIST_NAME at 09:00. Specs run alphabetically under workers:1, so marcacao-patient-link always took the slot first and PL-02 (a) always hit a genuine therapist double-booking. The single Guardar click got a real conflict refusal. THE PRODUCT WAS CORRECT TO REFUSE IT; the test was wrong to ask.

WHY IT READ AS INTERMITTENT FOR WEEKS: retries: CI ? 2 : 0 masked it. Attempt 1 collided; retry 1 shifted the day by +100, found an empty day and passed, so the suite went green. It surfaced only on a workflow_dispatch proving run, where the retries input defaults to 0. The retry was never re-running this test, it was running a different one.

HOW IT WAS SETTLED, after three wrong theories including two of my own: by extracting the failure webm from the artifact and reading it FRAME BY FRAME. At t~1.5s, before any submit, the agenda already showed the appointment. That killed the assumption every earlier theory rested on, which was that the drawer had created the row.

FIX: this spec moves to a PRIVATE day band 51-55 (51-69 was unused; the next occupied offsets are 70, 80, 90). That clears the exact collision at 45 and the four shared days at 40, 41, 42 and 44 in one move. Offsets are hand-assigned and nothing enforces uniqueness, so the header now tells the next editor to grep before adding one: a shared DAY is only safe when the time or the therapist differs.

HONEST NOTE ON THE VERIFICATION: my FIRST proving run was worthless and I am recording that rather than quietly re-running. Its --grep filter did not match the colliding spec, so only PL-02 (a) ran. With nobody taking the slot it would have passed even unfixed. The evidence on this card is the FULL-suite run where both specs execute together.

evidence.ref: OWNER ATTESTATION 2026-08-03 - 'migration was applied'. NOT an independent read. Receipt half: PR #751 merged (commit 0b4ce3c), migration file 0052_conflicts_no_show_releases_slot.sql present on main, blocking-status.test.ts pins the SQL and the app predicate to the same set so a half-landing is red CI. To UPGRADE to a receipt, record the __drizzle_migrations count delta 51 -> 52 on dfotoodqvmjhbdcxyaxf, or a read of appointment_conflicts() showing NOT IN ('cancelled','no_show') in both branches.

cards.notes:
ADDED TO THE BOARD 2026-08-03 by GREEN during orientation. This card did not exist: PR #751 merged migration 0052 plus its app-layer predicate to main, tagged [HOLD: migration], and no card tracked it in either direction. 47 cards and none covered it. That is how a merged migration with an outstanding prod apply becomes invisible.

WHAT IT DOES (owner ruling S1). The blocking set for double-booking becomes scheduled + confirmed + completed. Both cancelled AND no_show now release the slot: the patient did not attend, so the therapist was in fact free, and the row is history rather than an occupation. completed stays blocking on conservative grounds - overlapping a completed session is always a data error.

TWO SITES, ONE RULE. The predicate lives in the DB function public.appointment_conflicts() (changed by 0052) and in the app layer at apps/api/lib/appointments/store.ts (changed in the same PR). blocking-status.test.ts reads BOTH as text and fails if they express different sets, so landing either half alone turns CI red by design. That guard covers the REPO. It cannot see prod: the app half goes live on deploy, the DB half only on apply. Until the apply, the two disagree and the DB is the stricter of the pair.

WHY IT IS SHIPPED ON AN ATTESTATION. The owner confirmed the apply on 2026-08-03 when asked directly. Per board doctrine that is an attestation, not a receipt, and it is labelled as one in the evidence field. It is the same grade of proof as G1 and G4..G9. The count-delta read named in the evidence would settle it in one line.

NO PAST-DATE EXPOSURE (verified in the migration header, not assumed). Freeing a past no_show does not make a past date bookable by a patient: the slot sweep is floored three times over in store.ts listOpenSlots (day grid from now::date forward, `where s.starts_at > now`, and slot_in_past thrown on submit). Staff availability is deliberately not floored so staff can record a past walk-in, so a past no_show now reads as free in the STAFF agenda. That is the intended meaning of the ruling and grants staff nothing they did not already have.

cards.title: NIF mandatory on ficha creation - a valid PT NIF, or an explicit 'sem NIF' exemption with a reason (MIGRATION, apply-before-merge)

evidence.ref: PR #759 merged 2026-08-03T16:17:25Z on full green CI (Playwright E2E 13m32s - a real run, DB-gated 2m37s, lint+typecheck+test 1m59s, 1591 unit tests, all three Vercel builds). MIGRATION 0053: owner ran the guarded apply script, which refuses to proceed without AUTORIZO and re-reads prod afterwards. GREEN CAPTURED THE PRE-APPLY READ DIRECTLY: applied count 52, nif_exempt absent, nif_exempt_reason absent, constraint absent, target aws-0-eu-central-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432 - and the three most recent tracking rows matched the journal timestamps for 0050/0051/0052, which is what identifies it as the NEW prod. The POST-apply read was run by the owner and is NOT captured here; the merge is the receipt that he saw it.

cards.notes:
Owner CR 2026-08-03, verbatim: "when creating ficha clinica, the NIF field must be as mandatory to fill in, cannot move forward without it".

TWO THINGS IN THE CODE MADE THIS A DECISION RATHER THAN A ONE-LINE CHANGE, and both were put to the owner before any build.

1. NIF IS FREE TEXT TODAY. validation.ts:184 is optionalText(nif, 20) - no format check at all, so "abc" saves fine. Mandatory-as-non-empty would produce a required field full of "0" and "-", which is worse than optional because it looks trustworthy. But a real PT NIF check has a cost: foreign patients do not have one, and a hard block with no escape means reception literally cannot register a foreign walk-in, so they invent a number and nothing records that they did.
   OWNER RULING: valid PT NIF (9 digits + mod-11 checksum), WITH an explicit "Estrangeiro / sem NIF" exemption that requires a written reason. The exemption is recorded on the patient, so every exception is auditable instead of hiding as an empty field.

2. THERE IS A SECOND CREATE PATH. consultation/actions.ts:46 createStubPatientAction quick-creates a patient from name + optional phone so a therapist can start recording a walk-in immediately. Enforcing NIF inside the shared parseCreatePatient would have killed that flow silently.
   OWNER RULING: the stub path stays name + phone. The patient is instead marked FICHA INCOMPLETA (derived, not a column: nif IS NULL AND NOT nif_exempt), shows a warning on the patient page, and cannot have a declaracao or fatura issued until the NIF is supplied. The rule binds where it matters fiscally without blocking clinical work at the worst possible moment.

SCOPE. Presence is enforced on CREATE only - the owner said "when creating". Existing NIF-less patients stay editable, otherwise this change would brick every legacy ficha. Two smaller rules ride along because without them the requirement is defeated in one click: any NIF supplied on UPDATE must also be well-formed, and a patient who HAS a NIF cannot have it cleared back to empty on update (checked in the action, where the current row is available; a patient who never had one is untouched by this).

MIGRATION 0053 (this card authors it; the OWNER applies it): patients gains nif_exempt boolean not null default false, and nif_exempt_reason text. One CHECK: exempt implies a reason. Safe on existing rows - they all land nif_exempt=false, so the check passes trivially and nothing is backfilled or locked. GREEN never applies it: build, CI green, owner applies from the osteojp-prod-apply worktree with git checkout origin/<branch> detached, independent read of both columns plus the __drizzle_migrations count delta, THEN merge.

NOTE ON THE NUMBER: 0053 is taken by THIS card because it is being built first. PL-26 previously reserved 0053 in its notes and has been corrected again - numbers follow build order, not reservations.

BLAST RADIUS, known before starting: every Playwright spec that creates a patient (~12 call sites across patients.spec, notes-unification.spec, patient-documents.spec) goes through the e2e createPatient helper, which fills NIF only when asked. The helper must supply a valid generated NIF by default or the whole suite reds out on a change that is working correctly.

BUILT 2026-08-03, AWAITING THE OWNER'S MIGRATION APPLY. Status is BLOCKED, not shipped, and deliberately so: 0053 is authored but NOT on prod, and a card whose database half has not landed is not done however green its CI is.

WHAT IS ON THE BRANCH: migration 0053 (+ supabase mirror + journal), the nif.ts validator (checksum, prefix rule, consumidor-final rejection, isFichaIncomplete), server enforcement in parseCreatePatient/parseUpdatePatient, the no-clearing rule in updatePatient, the form with the exemption checkbox and its required reason, the ficha-incompleta banner, the declaracao block, PT+EN strings, 26 new unit tests, and a new e2e spec.

GATES RUN LOCALLY AND GREEN: lint (0 errors), typecheck (9/9 packages), unit tests (1588 web tests pass), the web production build, db:check, db:check-journal, db:sync-supabase:check.

GATES THAT COULD NOT RUN LOCALLY, STATED PLAINLY: the full pnpm build and pnpm test:e2e. This machine has no Supabase env vars, so the portal prerender and the Playwright webServer both die before reaching any of this work. Verified on a CLEAN TREE that both fail identically without these changes, so this is the environment and not the change - but it does mean nif-required.spec.ts has never executed, and CI is its first real run. If it reds, read the Playwright artifact before touching the spec.

OWNER'S MOVE, in order: (1) apply 0053 from the osteojp-prod-apply worktree using git checkout origin/patients/PL-31-nif-mandatory in DETACHED head - on main, db:migrate silently no-ops; (2) independent read of both new columns plus the __drizzle_migrations count delta 52 -> 53; (3) then merge. Applying before merge is the rule here because the app half ships on deploy and the DB half does not.

TWO QUESTIONS LOGGED, NEITHER BLOCKING: Q-PL-31-1 (do existing NIF-less patients need an active backfill push, or is the banner enough - needs a prod count GREEN cannot take) and Q-PL-31-2 (should invoicing block on a missing NIF too - left alone deliberately, since invoicing legal compliance is owner-confirmable and a fatura to consumidor final is legal in PT).

CI RUN 1 WENT RED AND CAUGHT A REAL BUG OF MINE - the exact one this card's own notes said to avoid. createStubPatientAction routes through createPatient, so enforcing the NIF inside the shared parseCreatePatient blocked EVERY consultation walk-in stub. consultation-start.spec.ts failed outright. The design was right and the implementation contradicted it in the same session.

FIX: two server actions, not a flag. createPatient requires the NIF; createStubPatient does not; both call a private impl. A flag on the exported action would have been a client-supplied bypass - this file is "use server", so any browser could have posted requireNif:false. The bypass is presence-only: a NIF supplied to the stub path is still format-checked. Four unit tests pin it so it cannot regress silently.

FOUR OTHER RED TESTS, three my test bugs and one a fixture that was never real: patients.spec.ts used nif "900000001", which is NOT a valid NIF (its control digit should be 7) - a fake fixture nothing had ever checked; the e2e NIF default sat in createPatient while two specs call fillPatientForm directly, so it moved into fillPatientForm keyed off the input's own required property; one assertion matched the NIF twice (it also appears in the identity line); and two of my cases hand-filled name + NIF without choosing a clinic, which is REQUIRED - the browser blocked the submit on its own validation so the request never reached the server, and they proved nothing while looking like they did.

CI RUN 2 IS FULLY GREEN: Playwright E2E 13m56s (a real run, not a docs-only skip), DB-gated tests 2m37s, lint+typecheck+test 2m7s, all three Vercel deployments built. Unit tests 1591 pass.

SHIPPED 2026-08-03. Owner applied 0053 and merged #759.

EVIDENCE GRADE, stated honestly: the merge and the CI run are receipts. The prod apply is one step weaker - GREEN captured the BEFORE read (count 52, both columns absent) but not the AFTER. The apply script re-reads prod and prints the verdict, and the owner merged after seeing it, so the inference is strong; it is still an inference. One safe command upgrades it to a receipt, and it can be run at any time:
  cd ~/Documents/Projects/GitHub/osteojp-prod-apply
  set -a; . ~/osteojp-secrets/new-prod.env; set +a
  node ~/osteojp-mailbox/staged/green-pl31-verify-0053-READONLY-20260803.mjs

PROD IMPACT MEASURED IN THE PRE-APPLY READ: 12 active patients, 6 with no NIF. Those six now show 'Ficha incompleta' and cannot have a declaracao issued until a NIF or an exemption is recorded. That number ANSWERS Q-PL-31-1: six is small enough to clear at the desk as those patients next attend, so no backfill ticket is needed and none was written.

cards.title: Editing an appointment saves the non-time fields BEFORE checking the new time is free, so a conflict leaves a half-applied edit
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-05 while root-causing LE-marcacoes-tab-edit-flake. Real product bug, verified in code, NOT a test issue.

WHERE: apps/web/app/agenda/appointment-drawer.tsx submit(). Two sequential server calls with no shared transaction:
  1. updateAppointment(editing.id, patch, ...) writes and COMMITS the non-temporal patch: serviceId, room, notes, status.
  2. THEN, if the date/time/therapist/location changed, rescheduleAppointment(...) runs and CAN return a conflict. handleResult returns false and submit() returns early, WITHOUT succeed().

WHAT THE USER SEES: they open a booking, change the service AND move it onto a slot that turns out to be occupied. The drawer stays open showing a conflict and a 'Guardar mesmo assim' override. Everything about that screen says nothing was saved. The service change is ALREADY LIVE. If they press Cancelar, believing they backed out, the change stays.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: reception is the heaviest user of this drawer, and 'I cancelled out of it' is the normal reaction to a conflict warning. The record then disagrees with what the person believes they did, which is the same class of problem as a booking that silently does not save.

RECOMMENDED FIX (owner decision, hence owner_merge): do the conflict check BEFORE committing the patch, so one refusal means nothing was written. Either move the availability/conflict check ahead of updateAppointment, or put both writes behind one server action in a single transaction. The second is cleaner and matches how createAppointment already behaves: it returns on conflict BEFORE its INSERT.

NOT FIXED in PR #789, which is deliberately test-only.

FIXED IN PR #792, awaiting merge. The reschedule now runs BEFORE the patch, because the reschedule is where conflicts come from, so a refusal leaves nothing written. That is what the conflict banner already implied and now it is true. The residual case (a room double-booking at the new time, after the move committed) is no longer silent: a new string tells the user the appointment WAS moved and which changes did not save. NOT marked shipped until #792 merges: an open PR is not evidence that anything landed. NOTE ON SCOPE: the complete fix is one server action in one transaction. That is a larger change to the busiest write path in the app and was deliberately not attempted here.

cards.title: Post-commit work sits inside the try that returns failure, so a SAVED booking can be reported to the user as an error
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-05 while root-causing LE-marcacoes-tab-edit-flake. Latent, not currently firing, but the shape is wrong.

WHERE: apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts createAppointment. After the transaction commits and result.ok is true, revalidatePath(AGENDA_PATH) and `await enqueueRemindersAfterCommit(...)` both run INSIDE the same try whose catch returns fail("create", e). If either throws, the caller receives a failure for an appointment that IS saved. The same shape repeats in cloneAppointment, updateAppointment and rescheduleAppointment.

WHAT THE USER WOULD SEE: 'erro' on a booking that actually exists. The natural response at the desk is to book it again, which produces a real double-booking. That is strictly worse than the error it is reporting.

WHY IT IS ONLY LATENT TODAY: enqueueRemindersAfterCommit try/catches each individual send internally, so only a ReminderBurstError escapes, and a single create has one target. revalidatePath rarely throws. So the path is reachable but not currently exercised, which is exactly the kind of bug that waits for a bad day.

RECOMMENDED FIX: move the post-commit work out of the try, or wrap it in its own try/catch that logs and still returns ok. A committed write must never be reported as a failure. Cheap, low risk, and it removes a double-booking route.

NOT FIXED in PR #789, which is deliberately test-only.

FIXED IN PR #792, awaiting merge. New afterCommit() helper wraps all four post-commit sites (create, clone, update, reschedule), so a committed write can never be reported as a failure. Errors are swallowed because the write is durable and every caller is best-effort, and logged with the step name and the error NAME only, never the message or a payload (rule 7). Four unit tests pin it, including one asserting a genuine TRANSACTION failure still returns not-ok, so the guard cannot paper over a real one. NOT marked shipped until #792 merges.

cards.title: agenda-cards.spec.ts:104 (three same-slot appointments stack vertically) fails at --retries=0
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-05 in the full-suite proving run 30986393217 (--retries=0) for PR #789. NOT caused by that PR, which is a test-only day-band change in a different spec, and NOT related to the marcacoes collision.

SYMPTOM: getByRole("button", { name: /Joao Pereira/ }) not found, 8s timeout, test takes 18.9s. So one of the three same-slot appointments it books never appeared on the agenda.

WHY IT HAS BEEN INVISIBLE: the suite runs retries: CI ? 2 : 0, so this is normally retried and goes green. It is the SECOND test found hiding behind retries in two days. That is the pattern worth acting on, not just this one test.

DO NOT THEORISE. Read the Playwright artifact from run 30986393217 first: the video and error-context named the cause outright for the marcacoes flake after three wrong theories, two of them mine.

ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED IN PR #793, awaiting merge. Read the artifact first, as the doctrine says, and it named the cause outright: the page snapshot shows the chosen date 17/01/2027 against a week grid rendering '11 a 16 de janeiro'. 17/01/2027 is a SUNDAY, and the agenda week view is Mon-Sat (W3-08), so a Sunday date renders the PRECEDING week and the three appointments just booked were genuinely not in view. The locator was right and the page was right; the test picked a day the view cannot show. RUN_DAY_BASE is randomised per run, so it landed on a Sunday roughly one run in seven, and retries hid it because a retry re-derives the same calendar date. New futureWeekdayDate() in e2e/fixtures.ts steps a Sunday to the Monday. NOT marked shipped until #793 merges.
